tasks.title: WB-101 Finish Saved Views — apply saved filters on the Tasks page
tasks.description:
Saved Views currently have full CRUD (domain model, repository, hooks, page at `/saved-views`)
but a saved view's `filters` object is never applied anywhere. This is the one half-built
feature in the app and the highest-value quick win: it closes the gap without new domain work.

Applying a view should push its filters into the Tasks page URL query state so the existing
filter/sort/pagination machinery does the rest.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [x] Selecting a saved view from `/saved-views` or the Tasks toolbar navigates to `/tasks` with the view's filters encoded in the URL.
- [x] Applying a view sets search, status, priority, project, due, tags, sort and order exactly as stored.
- [x] The active view name is visible on the Tasks page and can be cleared back to the default state.
- [x] A "Save current filters as view" action on the Tasks page creates a view from the live URL state.
- [x] Applying a view is keyboard accessible and announced to assistive tech.
- [x] Unit tests cover the URL <-> filters mapping; an E2E test covers apply + clear.

- `SavedView.filters` already mirrors the Tasks URL param names (`q`, `status`, `priority`, `project`, `due`, `sort`, `order`, `tags`), so no schema migration is needed.
- Keep filter state URL-driven (see `CASE_STUDY.md` Decision 1); do not introduce a second source of truth.
- Tag filtering was wired into the Tasks filter bar as toggle chips (multi-select); a view's `tags` array round-trips through the `tags` URL param.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-101-finish-saved-views.md

Source: competitor-analysis

tasks.title: WB-102 Add sub-tasks (parent/child tasks)
tasks.description:
Workboard has a flat task model, so there is no way to break a task into smaller steps.
Sub-tasks are the single most requested capability on a "serious" task tool and the clearest
gap versus Jira, Linear and Asana. This adds a self-referential parent/child relationship.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [x] `Task` gains an optional `parentId?: string` (a task id) with validation that the parent exists and is not itself a child (max depth of one level).
- [x] A task with children displays a progress indicator (done / total) in list and Kanban views.
- [x] Tasks with a `parentId` are hidden from the top-level board/list by default, with a toggle to show them.
- [x] Creating, editing and deleting a parent updates its children safely (deleting a parent either blocks with a warning or cascades to trash — decide and document).
- [x] IndexedDB records remain backward compatible (missing `parentId` is valid).
- [x] Domain, repository, and component tests cover nesting, depth limits and cascade behaviour.

- Keep the storage schema additive; no migration should be required because `parentId` is optional.
- Reuse the existing trash/soft-delete semantics for cascades rather than hard deletes.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-102-sub-tasks.md

Source: readme-gaps

tasks.title: WB-103 Add task dependencies (blocked by / blocks)
tasks.description:
There is no way to express that one task blocks another. Dependencies are a core planning
primitive in Jira and Linear and let the app flag work that cannot start yet.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `Task` gains `blockedBy: string[]` (task ids), validated against existing tasks.
- [ ] A task shows a "Blocked" indicator when any blocking task is not `done`.
- [ ] The Task form lets a user add/remove blockers with keyboard support.
- [ ] Cycles are prevented (A blocks B blocks A is rejected with a clear error).
- [ ] Blocked tasks are visually distinct in list and Kanban views.
- [ ] A dependency filter is available on the Tasks page (e.g. `blocked=true`).
- [ ] Domain and component tests cover cycle rejection and blocked-state derivation.

- Derive blocked state in a pure domain function; do not store a redundant "isBlocked" flag.
- This is additive to `WB-102`; both touch the task domain model, so sequence them to avoid churn.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-103-task-dependencies.md

Source: readme-gaps

tasks.title: WB-104 Add CSV and Markdown export plus a printable board
tasks.description:
JSON export/import exists, but it is machine-oriented. Reinforce Workboard's data-ownership
story with human-friendly outputs: CSV for spreadsheets, Markdown for docs and status reports,
and a print/PDF view of a board.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Settings offers CSV export of tasks (and projects) with stable column headers and RFC 4180 escaping.
- [ ] Settings offers Markdown export of the current backlog (reuse the BACKLOG.md table shape).
- [ ] A print stylesheet renders the project board and task list cleanly for PDF (no nav chrome).
- [ ] Export actions are keyboard accessible and announce completion.
- [ ] Round-trip unit tests prove exported CSV parses back to the same values.
- [ ] Documentation in README and `docs/project-management.md` describes each format.

- Keep generation in a pure function so it is unit-testable without the DOM.
- Reuse `date-fns` formatting already used in the app; do not hand-roll date strings.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-104-csv-markdown-export.md

Source: competitor-analysis

tasks.title: WB-201 Spike — optional self-hostable sync behind the repository interface
tasks.description:
Workboard's biggest gap versus Jira, Trello and Linear is collaboration and multi-device use.
Rather than surrender the offline/local-first identity, add an **optional, self-hostable** sync
path implemented behind the existing `IProjectRepository` / `ITaskRepository` interfaces. This is
a timeboxed spike to de-risk the approach before committing to a build.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A written spike report documents the options (CRDT via Yjs/Automerge vs a small REST API vs WebSocket relay) with trade-offs for an offline-first app.
- [ ] A working prototype demonstrates `ApiRepository` (or a sync layer) satisfying the same repository contract used by hooks.
- [ ] The prototype proves optimistic updates and the `Result<T, E>` error model still hold when a network is involved.
- [ ] A recommendation with effort estimate and a migration path is recorded in `docs/decisions/`.
- [ ] No change to existing behaviour when sync is disabled (local-only remains the default).

- `docs/architecture.md` already lists "Swap LocalRepository → ApiRepository" as the intended extension point; validate that claim with real code.
- Bedrock constraint: existing components and hooks must not change.
- Explicitly out of scope: hosted SaaS, accounts, billing.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-201-sync-spike.md

Source: competitor-analysis

tasks.title: WB-202 Add a calendar view
tasks.description:
Due dates exist but can only be seen in a list. A calendar (month/week) view is table stakes in
Trello Premium and Asana and makes due dates actionable.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A `/calendar` route renders tasks by `dueDate` in a month grid, with a week view.
- [ ] Tasks are grouped and colour-coded by project; overdue tasks are visually distinct.
- [ ] Clicking a day shows that day's tasks; clicking a task opens the task detail.
- [ ] View state (range, project filter) is stored in the URL for shareable links.
- [ ] Fully keyboard navigable and screen-reader friendly (grid semantics, roving tabindex or equivalent).
- [ ] Empty and no-due-date states are handled explicitly.
- [ ] Component tests for date bucketing; one E2E journey.

- Reuse the existing date utilities and design tokens; do not add a calendar dependency unless the a11y story is verified.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-202-calendar-view.md

Source: competitor-analysis

tasks.title: WB-203 Add a timeline / roadmap view
tasks.description:
A horizontal timeline showing tasks or epics across time gives planning context that the board
and list lack. This is a common reason teams move to Asana or Monday.com.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A `/timeline` route renders project rows and task bars positioned by due date (and a start date if added later).
- [ ] Bars scale across day/week/month zoom levels with a "today" marker.
- [ ] Overdue and completed tasks are visually distinct; hovering/focusing a bar summarises the task.
- [ ] Project and status filters apply, driven by the URL like other views.
- [ ] Keyboard navigable; bars are focusable and announce their dates.
- [ ] Handles empty projects and tasks without dates gracefully.
- [ ] Component tests for the date-to-pixel scaling maths.

- Depends conceptually on `WB-102` (parent/child) if timelines should roll up epics; can ship task-only first.
- Keep the layout CSS-based; avoid a heavy Gantt library to protect the bundle budget.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-203-timeline-view.md

Source: competitor-analysis

tasks.title: WB-204 Add basic reporting — cycle time, throughput and overdue trend
tasks.description:
The dashboard shows point-in-time counts. Add simple, trend-based reporting so the app is
useful for reflection, not just task entry.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Reports show throughput (tasks completed per week) over a selectable range.
- [ ] Cycle time (created → completed) is reported per project over the range.
- [ ] An overdue trend chart shows counted-overdue tasks over time.
- [ ] All metrics are computed by pure domain functions from stored timestamps (`createdAt`, `completedAt`, `dueDate`).
- [ ] Charts are accessible: values available as text/table, not colour alone, and keyboard reachable.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the aggregation maths with fixed fixtures.
- [ ] No new runtime dependency if a small SVG implementation suffices within the bundle budget.

- Prefer dependency-free SVG charts; the app targets a ≤100 KB gzip JS budget.
- Be explicit that metrics are derived locally from user data and never uploaded.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-204-reporting.md

Source: competitor-analysis

tasks.title: WB-301 Add file attachments stored in IndexedDB
tasks.description:
Tasks cannot hold files. Attachments are expected in every comparable tool. Store blobs locally
in IndexedDB so the offline, no-upload promise is preserved.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A task can hold zero or more attachments (name, type, size, blob).
- [ ] Files are stored in a dedicated IndexedDB object store; metadata is validated with Zod.
- [ ] A configurable per-file size limit and total-quota guard surface clear errors on `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`.
- [ ] Attachments can be added via drag-and-drop and a file picker, downloaded, and removed.
- [ ] Non-text files never render inline; downloads use safe `Content-Disposition` behaviour.
- [ ] Import/export clearly states that attachments are local-only (see `WB-404` for the export gap).
- [ ] Tests cover add/remove and error paths; the storage adapter's failure injection is exercised.

- Keep blobs out of the JSON export by default to avoid multi-megabyte backups; document the trade-off.
- Consider whether attachments live in the trash lifecycle with their task.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-301-file-attachments.md

Source: readme-gaps

tasks.title: WB-302 Support recurring tasks
tasks.description:
Tasks that repeat (daily, weekly, monthly, custom interval) are unsupported. They are common
for maintenance and routine work.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `Task` gains an optional recurrence rule (frequency + interval + optional until date).
- [ ] Completing a recurring task schedules the next occurrence rather than ending the series.
- [ ] Recurrence is validated in the domain and rendered in the task form and list.
- [ ] The next occurrence is computed by a pure, timezone-safe domain function.
- [ ] A series can be stopped; past occurrences are retained as history.
- [ ] Tests cover interval maths, DST/timezone edges, and completion behaviour.

- Keep the rule shape simple (RFC 5545 RRULE is likely overkill); document the subset supported.
- All dates in the app are calendar dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`); preserve that convention.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-302-recurring-tasks.md

Source: readme-gaps

tasks.title: WB-303 Add due-date reminders and in-app notifications
tasks.description:
The app surfaces overdue tasks passively on the dashboard. Add reminders so upcoming due dates
reach the user without them opening the app.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A notifications centre lists tasks that are due soon or overdue.
- [ ] Optional browser notifications are requested and scheduled with user consent, degrading gracefully when denied.
- [ ] Users can configure a lead time (e.g. remind 1 day before due).
- [ ] Preferences persist with the existing settings repository.
- [ ] No network calls; scheduling is local (Notification API / service worker if `WB-305` lands first).
- [ ] Tests cover the "which tasks are due for a reminder" pure function.

- Depends on `WB-305` (PWA/service worker) for reliable background reminders; in-app list can ship first.
- Respect the reduced-motion and accessibility conventions used by toasts.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-303-reminders.md

Source: readme-gaps

tasks.title: WB-304 Design a public API and webhooks for automation
tasks.description:
Workboard has no integration surface, which blocks automation and dev-tool wiring where Jira and
Linear excel. The local-first architecture makes a hosted API a product decision, so start with a
design spike rather than an implementation.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A design document defines resources, endpoints, auth model, and versioning.
- [ ] At least one concrete integration scenario is walked through end-to-end (e.g. create task from a webhook payload).
- [ ] The proposal states how a public API coexists with the offline/local-only default, including a self-hosted option.
- [ ] Security review covers auth, rate limiting, and data exposure for a client-owned data model.
- [ ] The recommendation is captured in `docs/decisions/` with an explicit decision on build vs defer.

- This is deliberately a spike: it depends on the sync decision in `WB-201`.
- Do not expose user data without an explicit, documented consent model.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-304-public-api.md

Source: competitor-analysis

tasks.title: WB-305 Ship a PWA with install and encrypted local backup
tasks.description:
Workboard works offline in the browser but is not installable. A PWA makes the offline-first
promise tangible and closes part of the platform gap with native apps.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A service worker precaches the app shell and assets; the app loads offline after first visit.
- [ ] A web app manifest (name, icons, theme colours) enables install on desktop and mobile.
- [ ] An update flow prompts the user to reload when a new version is available.
- [ ] An optional encrypted backup exports data protected by a user passphrase (Web Crypto).
- [ ] Cache strategy is documented and does not break SPA deep links.
- [ ] Lighthouse PWA checks pass and no performance budget regressions.

- Coordinate with `WB-303` (notifications) which benefits from a service worker.
- Encryption must be documented clearly: a lost passphrase means lost data.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-305-pwa-encrypted-backup.md

Source: competitor-analysis

tasks.title: WB-401 Add epics / milestones above tasks
tasks.description:
Workboard's model is Project → Task. Jira and Linear add a planning tier (epic / milestone) above
tasks, which is essential for grouping work and rolling up progress. This is the largest
product-model gap versus the enterprise tools.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [x] Domain (`src/domain/epic.ts`) with `Epic` / `EpicInput`; `Task` gained optional `epicId`; `validation.ts` adds schemas + import/export/relationships; `epicRepository` with CRUD + detach-on-delete via `useDeleteEpic`; hooks `useEpics`/`useCreateEpic`/`useUpdateEpic`/`useDeleteEpic`; `migrations` exports/imports/clears `epics`.
- [x] Epics appear on the project detail view with rolled-up progress (done / total, % complete).
- [x] Tasks can be assigned to an epic in the task form; unassigned tasks remain valid.
- [x] An epic filter is available on the Tasks page and in saved views.
- [x] Deleting an epic detaches tasks rather than deleting them (documented behaviour).
- [x] Schema change is additive and backward compatible; migrations tested.
- [x] Domain and component tests cover roll-ups and detach-on-delete.

- Sequence with `WB-102` (sub-tasks) to avoid two competing hierarchy mechanisms.
- Decide and document the relationship: is an epic also a task type, or a separate entity? Recommendation: separate entity for clarity.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-401-epics-milestones.md

Source: competitor-analysis

tasks.title: WB-402 Add comments and an activity feed
tasks.description:
Every comparable tool lets you annotate work and see what changed. Workboard has neither
comments nor an audit trail. Even single-user, a per-task activity log improves recall and
forms the foundation for future collaboration.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A task detail view shows a dated comment thread and a change history (status, priority, assignee, due date).
- [ ] Comments and activity entries are persisted with the task or in a related store.
- [ ] Changes made through the app (and via import) produce activity entries.
- [ ] The feed is accessible: ordered list semantics, timestamps in readable form.
- [ ] Tests cover activity generation on update and rendering of an empty thread.

- Design the record shape so it can later carry an author id when accounts arrive (`WB-201` sync, future auth).
- Keep the activity log out of the compact JSON export unless `WB-404` decides otherwise.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-402-comments-activity.md

Source: competitor-analysis

tasks.title: WB-403 Virtualize long lists and raise the ~10k-task scale ceiling
tasks.description:
`README.md` lists "~10,000 tasks before performance degrades" as a known limitation because all
records are loaded and filtered in memory. Virtualize rendering and move pagination to the
repository layer so the app stays smooth at scale.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [x] Task and project lists render with windowing so DOM node count stays bounded.
- [x] A repository-level paged query avoids loading every record for list views.
- [x] Filtering/sorting remain correct and instant for datasets of at least 50k tasks (documented benchmark).
- [x] A repeatable benchmark script records render and filter timings in `docs/performance.md`.
- [x] No regression to keyboard navigation, focus order, or the a11y axe checks.
- [x] Update the "Known Limitations" section of README once the ceiling is raised.

- `docs/performance.md` already anticipates virtualization "if measured"; this ticket makes it measured and required.
- Keep the public filter/sort/paginate domain functions; change where they run, not what they do.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-403-virtualization-scale.md

Source: readme-gaps

tasks.title: WB-404 Include labels and saved views in export/import
tasks.description:
Foundation: the app exposes Labels and Saved Views, and both have repositories and full CRUD,
but the backup format silently omits them. `exportDataSchema` / `importDataSchema`
(`src/domain/validation.ts`) only cover `projects`, `tasks` and `settings`, and
`exportAllData` / `importData` (`src/infrastructure/storage/migrations.ts`) never touch the
label or saved-view stores. A user who exports, clears, and re-imports loses their labels and
saved views without warning. That breaks the data-ownership promise.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [x] The export payload includes `labels` and `savedViews` (optional fields for backward compatibility with existing backups).
- [x] Import restores labels and saved views, respecting merge vs replace semantics consistently with projects/tasks.
- [x] Older backups without those fields still import successfully.
- [x] Relationship validation covers any cross-references (e.g. a saved view referencing a label).
- [x] Export/import round-trip tests include labels and saved views, plus a legacy-payload test.
- [x] README documents exactly what a backup contains.

- Verify how labels and saved views are keyed in storage (`workboard:labels:*`, `workboard:savedViews:*`) before wiring `getAll`/`set`.
- This is a correctness bug disguised as a feature gap; treat it as high priority despite the small surface area.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-404-export-labels-saved-views.md

Source: code-audit

tasks.title: WB-501 Publish a competitor analysis (Jira, Trello, Linear)
tasks.description:
The project lacked any market context. Add a competitor analysis positioning Workboard against
Jira (the enterprise anchor) and its two closest analogs — Trello (scope) and Linear
(interaction quality) — and derive a roadmap from the findings.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [x] `COMPETITOR_ANALYSIS.md` documents positioning, a feature matrix, and dimension-by-dimension analysis.
- [x] The two "best similar products" are justified (Trello for scope, Linear for UX), with Jira as the requested anchor.
- [x] Honest gaps and a tiered roadmap are derived from the analysis.
- [x] The README links to the analysis.
- [x] Sources and 2026 pricing notes are included.

- Sources are third-party pricing/comparison pages from 2026; treat figures as approximate.
- Follow-up work derived from this analysis is tracked in the roadmap and product-gap projects.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-501-competitor-analysis.md

Source: competitor-analysis

tasks.title: WB-502 Establish a ticket system with a machine-readable backlog
tasks.description:
Work needs a durable home that both humans and agents can read. Drive the backlog from canonical
markdown tickets (`tickets/WB-*.md`) with flat YAML frontmatter, and generate a human/agent index
(`BACKLOG.md`) plus a Workboard-importable snapshot from that single source of truth.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [x] A ticket format is defined (frontmatter fields, allowed values, tag taxonomy) and documented.
- [x] `scripts/tickets-build.mjs` deterministically generates `project-management/workboard-import.json` and `BACKLOG.md` from `tickets/WB-*.md`.
- [x] The generated import validates against the app's own Zod import schema (projects, tasks, tags, statuses, dates).
- [x] A `--check` mode fails when generated artifacts are stale.
- [x] A machine-readable `project-management/ticket.schema.json` describes the frontmatter for external tooling.
- [x] npm scripts `tickets:build` and `tickets:check` are wired up.

- Frontmatter is intentionally flat `key: value` scalars so parsing stays trivial and stable under formatting.
- Only `projects`, `tasks` and `settings` are importable; labels/saved views are a known export gap (`WB-404`).

Ticket file: tickets/WB-502-ticket-system.md

Source: product-management

tasks.title: WB-503 Add AGENTS.md and a documentation-as-code workflow
tasks.description:
Make the repository a first-class environment for AI agent teams. Add a root `AGENTS.md` that
agents read first, and a `docs/project-management.md` process doc that defines the ticket
workflow, sources of truth, and the rule that documentation and tickets are updated as part of
every change.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [x] `AGENTS.md` documents project overview, commands, architecture map, conventions, quality gates, and the ticket workflow.
- [x] `docs/project-management.md` defines sources of truth, ticket schema, tag taxonomy, status workflow, and the Workboard round-trip.
- [x] `STATUS.md` provides a living progress snapshot with an update rule.
- [x] The README links to the agent and project-management docs.
- [x] Documentation clearly states that updating tickets and markdown is part of the definition of done.

- `AGENTS.md` is the OpenCode/agent convention and is kept short, pointing to deeper docs.
- Keep the workflow tool-agnostic so non-OpenCode agent teams can follow it.

Ticket file: tickets/WB-503-agents-md-workflow.md

Source: product-management

tasks.title: WB-504 Enforce ticket/backlog sync in CI
tasks.description:
Generated artifacts drift the moment someone forgets to regenerate. Wire `tickets:check` into the
local `ci` script and the GitHub Actions workflow so stale tickets or a stale backlog fail the
build.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [x] `npm run tickets:check` verifies `BACKLOG.md` and `workboard-import.json` are up to date.
- [x] The check is part of the `ci` npm script.
- [x] The GitHub Actions `quality` job runs the check before tests.
- [x] Generated files are excluded from Prettier so `format:check` stays green.
- [x] The failure message tells the contributor exactly what to run.

- `--check` normalizes CRLF vs LF so the gate is reliable on Windows and Linux.
- Keep the check dependency-free and fast (no build required).

Ticket file: tickets/WB-504-ci-ticket-sync.md

tasks.title: WB-505 Add a Workboard-to-ticket sync script
tasks.description:
To dogfood Workboard as the daily driver, progress made in the app must flow back into the
canonical tickets. Add `scripts/tickets-sync.mjs` to fold a Workboard export back into ticket
frontmatter (status, priority, assignee, updated) and append an update-log entry.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [x] The script accepts a Workboard export JSON path and matches tasks to tickets by `WB-###` title prefix.
- [x] Status, priority, assignee and updated date are written back to the correct ticket files.
- [x] A dated entry is appended to `## Updates` when the status changes.
- [x] Trashed tasks (`deletedAt`) and unmatched tickets are reported, not silently ignored.

tasks.title: WB-506 Dev-only seeding of the Workboard backlog, no placeholder demo data
tasks.description:
`npm run dev` currently seeds three placeholder demo projects ("Website Redesign", "Mobile App
v2", "Q3 Marketing Campaign") and 11 fake tasks on first launch, and Settings offers a "Reset to
Demo" action that restores them. The placeholder data makes the app look like a generic demo
instead of the tool it actually is — and it ships its own dogfooding backlog already, generated
from `tickets/WB-*.md` into `project-management/workboard-import.json`.

Replace the demo seed with Workboard's own backlog (projects + tasks) and load it **only in
development**. Production builds start with an empty app — no placeholders anywhere.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [x] `createDemoData` / `demoData.ts`, `seedDemoData` and `resetToDemoData` are removed.
- [x] First `npm run dev` on a fresh profile seeds the 6 Workboard projects + their tasks from
      the generated `project-management/workboard-import.json`, validated through
      `importDataSchema` (`validateImportData`) before writing.
- [x] Seeding stays behind a static `import.meta.env.DEV` guard with a dynamic `import()` so the
      seed JSON never enters the production bundle; production builds start empty.
- [x] The existing `SEEDED_KEY` semantics are preserved (never re-seed after the user clears
      data).
- [x] Settings: "Reset to Demo" card, confirm dialog and `useResetDemoData` hook are removed;
      "Delete all data" remains the only destructive action.
- [x] Playwright runs against the dev server (seeded, dogfooded) instead of a preview build;
      E2E expectations reference real Workboard titles/tags.
- [x] Docs updated (`README`, `AGENTS`, `architecture`, `testing-strategy`, competitor analysis).
- [x] Gates green: format, lint, typecheck, tickets, unit tests, build, size, E2E.

- `project-management/workboard-import.json` is generated — never hand-edit; regenerate with
  `npm run tickets:build`.
- Free ticket id: WB-506 (WB-507 also free, WB-508 already taken).

Ticket file: tickets/WB-506-dev-seed-workboard-…

tasks.title: WB-507 Dev-only reseed so the Workboard backlog always comes back in development
tasks.description:
Since WB-506 the app seeds Workboard's own backlog on first launch — but only once per browser
profile (`workboard:meta:seeded`). Developers who already had that flag set from the old demo data,
or who delete their data while developing, end up with a permanently empty app and no obvious way
back short of clearing site data or hand-importing `workboard-import.json`.

Make development forgiving: in dev only, if the app has no projects, (re)import the backlog on
startup even when the seeded flag is already set. Production semantics are unchanged — it seeds
nothing and never re-seeds after a wipe.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [x] `initializeApp` re-seeds in development whenever there are zero projects, regardless of the
      seeded flag.
- [x] Production builds still seed nothing and never re-seed after `clearAllData`.
- [x] `loadDevSeed()` remains the single gate (`import.meta.env.DEV`) so no seed reaches `dist`.
- [x] Unit tests cover both paths (dev re-seeds; production does not).
- [x] Docs updated; gates green (format, lint, typecheck, tickets, unit tests, build, size, E2E).

- Follow-up to [WB-506](WB-506-dev-seed-workboard-backlog.md).
- Not a "Reset to Demo" revival: nothing in the UI changes, and production keeps the one-way
  behaviour.
